answers.2: It gives each retail credit card application a score and automatically declines the ones below a cutoff. It is for UK and German customers.
answers.4: Gives a score, ranking, flag, category or forecast — e.g. a credit score, a fraud alert, a ranking of CVs, the likely cause of a problem
5: Information about people — clients, applicants, staff or anyone else: names, contact details, account and financial details, CVs — anything about someone who can be identified
answers.6: acts by itself within limits someone set, with no routine review
answers.6b: Makes a yes-or-no decision — e.g. accepts or declines an application, signs something off
answers.7: Clients or customers — including people applying to us
answers.8: Whether to lend to someone, or on what terms
answers.10: Several teams, the whole business, or every case of a kind (e.g. all applications)

expectNext: I think the form will go on to step 4 'Questions'. That step may ask a few more things based on what I have answered, and step 5 'Confirm' lets me look over everything. Then step 6 'Result' tells me whether my colleague can go ahead with the credit card scoring model, and what has to be done first. I guess the answer comes from the firm's written rules, not from a person. Before that, 'Continue' might refuse to move on if any required answer is missing or any suggestion is not yet ticked. I'm not sure what the 'Similar checks' step does or whether I will see it.
ticksMean: The tool guessed some answers by reading my description, and each guess has an 'I've checked this answer' box. Ticking it means I have read the guess and agree it is right, so it now counts as my answer. Until I tick it, it doesn't count, I can't continue, and nobody can say the AI decided for me. If I disagree, I change the answer instead of ticking. I am the one responsible for the answers, not the AI model.
comment: I could do the form, but I had to say "Not sure" to several questions (where the AI comes from, whether a mistake can be put right, whether it replaces something, whether data stays in-house) because my colleague didn't tell me; the "question 6" reference and the unexplained "Similar checks" step were the confusing bits.
